questions.problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}\,i+\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-1)\,j+{e}^{t}\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}$ is $t\in [-2,2].$

- The domain of the 2nd component $\operatorname{ln}⁡(t-1)$ is $t\in (1,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component ${e}^{t}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14266735/assets/d43c856bf43fb3783a7ee34b2553879fdb99a791587f1c1e466bc135c868052d.png)

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is $t\in (1,2].$

questions.worked_solution:

- The domain of the 1st component $\operatorname{cos}⁡t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $\sqrt{2+{t}^{2}}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component $\operatorname{cot}⁡t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$, $t\ne n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is 

$$
t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),\,t\ne n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.
